title: 27.1 · Magnetic force on a negative charge
find: Find F for (a) B = 1.40 i T and (b) B = 1.40 k T.

steps.title: Part (a): field along x
steps.math: \mathbf v\times\mathbf B=-v_yB_x\mathbf k\\=-(-3.85\times10^4)(1.40)\mathbf k=5.390\times10^4\mathbf k\\\mathbf F=q(\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)=(-1.24\times10^{-8})(5.390\times10^4)\mathbf k\\\mathbf F=-6.68\times10^{-4}\mathbf k\ \mathrm N

steps.title: Part (b): field along z
steps.math: \mathbf v\times\mathbf B=B_z(v_y\mathbf i-v_x\mathbf j)\\=1.40[-3.85\times10^4\mathbf i-4.19\times10^4\mathbf j]\\\mathbf F=(-1.24\times10^{-8})(-5.390\times10^4\mathbf i-5.866\times10^4\mathbf j)\\\mathbf F=(6.68\mathbf i+7.27\mathbf j)\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm N

check: Each result is perpendicular to both velocity and field. A negative charge reverses the right-hand-rule direction.

title: 27.4 · Magnetic acceleration

steps.title: Take the cross product
steps.math: \mathbf v=v_y\mathbf j,\quad\mathbf B=B_x\mathbf i+B_y\mathbf j\\\mathbf v\times\mathbf B=-v_yB_x\mathbf k\\\mathbf a=\frac q m(\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)

check: j × i = −k, so acceleration is into the xy-plane for positive q.

title: 27.7 · Recover magnetic-field components
find: Find determined B components, identify any undetermined component, and calculate B·F and their angle.
answer: Bx = −0.175 T; Bz = −0.256 T; By undetermined; B·F = 0, angle 90°.
note: The force does not determine Bᵧ: a field parallel to the velocity adds no magnetic force.
check: B and F are perpendicular (90°) regardless of By. Do not assume By = 0 just because it is undetermined.

title: 27.19 · Cosmic-ray semicircle
given: Particles have |q| = 3e, m = 12mₚ and enter downward into B = 0.250 T out of the page. They curve to the right through a semicircle of diameter 0.950 m.
find: Find speed and charge sign, assess gravity, and compare entry/exit speeds.
answer: 2.84 × 10⁶ m/s; negative charge; negligible gravity; unchanged speed.
note: With velocity downward and B out of the page, positive charge would bend left. The shown path bends right, so the charge is negative.
check: Gravity is negligible. Magnetic force does no work, so entry and exit speeds are equal.

title: 27.21 · Deuteron orbit
given: Deuteron mass 3.34 × 10⁻²⁷ kg and charge +e; orbit radius 6.96 mm in B = 2.50 T.
find: Find speed, half-orbit time, and accelerating potential magnitude from rest.
check: The positive deuteron must move through a potential drop of 7.26 kV to gain this energy.

title: 27.24 · Quarter-circle proton path
given: Protons at 1.20 km/s turn 90° while travelling arc length 1.18 cm in a perpendicular magnetic field.
check: For a proton entering rightward and turning upward, B points into the page.

title: 27.27 · Crossed-field selector
given: v = +5.85 × 10³ j m/s; B = −1.35 k T. Charges are (a) +0.640 nC and (b) −0.320 nC.
find: Find E needed for undeflected motion in each case.

steps.title: Set the net force to zero
steps.math: q\mathbf E+q\mathbf v\times\mathbf B=0\\\mathbf E=-\mathbf v\times\mathbf B

steps.title: Substitute the velocity and field
steps.math: \mathbf v\times\mathbf B=(5.85\times10^3\mathbf j)\times(-1.35\mathbf k)\\=-7.8975\times10^3\mathbf i\\\mathbf E=+7.90\times10^3\mathbf i\ \mathrm{N/C}

check: Both forces reverse with charge sign, leaving the same cancellation condition.

title: 27.29 · Alpha-particle velocity selector
given: Alpha q = +2e, m = 6.64 × 10⁻²⁷ kg accelerates from rest through 1.75 kV. It enters rightward between plates separated 8.20 mm with 150 V across them; lower plate positive.
find: Find the magnetic field for no deflection.
check: B must point out of the page: rightward v × outward B points downward, cancelling the upward electric force. Plate area is not needed.
